entries.title: mkdir
entries.description: Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (`EEXIST` if it exists). The permissions are `mode & ~umask`; directories usually need the execute bits, e.g. `0755`.

entries.title: rmdir
entries.description: Returns 0 on success; fails with `ENOTEMPTY` if the directory is not empty.

entries.title: getcwd
entries.summary: Absolute path of the current working directory.
entries.description: Fills `buf` and returns it, or returns NULL on error (`ERANGE` if the buffer is too small).

entries.title: chdir
entries.summary: Change the current working directory of the program.
entries.description: Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. It changes the directory of YOUR process only: a program cannot change the directory of the shell that started it.
mistakes: Expecting the calling shell to change directory.

entries.title: opendir
entries.description: Returns a `DIR *` or NULL on error (not a directory, no permission…).
entries.example:
DIR *d = opendir(".");
if (d == NULL) { perror("."); return 1; }

entries.title: readdir
entries.summary: Next entry of an open directory.
entries.description: Returns the next entry, or NULL at the end. The name is `entry->d_name`. The order is arbitrary and includes `.` (the directory) and `..` (its parent): skip them with `strcmp` when you do not want them. The returned pointer is overwritten by the next call: copy the name (`strdup`) if you need it later.

entries.title: closedir
entries.summary: Close a directory opened with opendir.

entries.title: rewinddir
entries.summary: Go back to the first entry of an open directory.
entries.description: The next `readdir` returns the first entry again.
